name: Low-temperature UHV STM/STS of single Fe adatoms on cleaved Bi2Te3(111) at 4.5 K
plain_name: Image single iron atoms on a crystal surface with a microscope cooled to 4.5 K
description: A Bi2Te3 crystal is cleaved in ultrahigh vacuum, cooled to 4.5 K in the STM, dosed with about 0.2% of a monolayer of Fe from an in-situ e-beam evaporator while held at 4.5 K, then imaged and probed by lock-in dI/dV spectroscopy and mapping (877 Hz bias modulation).
keywords: Image single iron atoms on a crystal surface with a microscope cooled to 4.5 K

sources.citation: Nguyen D., Paudyal H., Sink J. R., Flatte M. E., Gupta J. A. Broken site symmetry of Fe adatoms on Bi2Te3. arXiv:2608.02770 (2026)

requirements.rationale: Imaging, spectroscopy and Fe deposition are all done with the sample at 4.5 K.
The cleaved surface and single adatoms require an ultrahigh-vacuum sample space.
Optional: the reported system pressure was 1e-11 mbar.
Tunnelling bias and lock-in modulation must be applied to the sample.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
